summary: This paper systematically sharpens the recent PPAD-completeness framework for exact normal-form correlated equilibrium (NFCE) in extensive-form games by Cheval, Horn, Paul, and Shirmohammadi (2026). Theorem 1 replaces the tree-wide denominator product B with the path-LCM L = lcm_{z,i} den(p_c(z) u_i(z)) and applies Cramer's rule with an unscaled simplex row and column-norm Hadamard estimation on the active support, halving the dimension exponent in the uniform LP gap and cutting oracle precision bit-budgets by 4.91x-26.96x on depth-2 to depth-6 benchmarks (with O(|Z|/h) asymptotic savings), alongside an exact 4L determinant bound and 1/(2L) realization at r=2. Theorem 2 proves the exact two-player collapse 2(K - kappa_d) = d_1^2 + d_2^2 + (d_1 - d_2)^2 and introduces the polynomial-time computable effective payoff-deviation rank r_i <= d_i, compressing the general n-player support bound to K_eff = min(prod_i(d_i+1), 1 + sum_i(d_i+1)r_i). Theorem 3 removes the power-of-two restriction on matching trees, shrinks PPAD-hardness tree sizes by 8.4x-15.9x (kappa_d) and 43.8x-86.5x (kappa_+), proves exact b-ary optimality (node slope 6 iff b in {2,3}, leaf slope 3 uniquely at b=2), establishes leaf-count PPAD-completeness under kappa_N = floor(N^2/9) for all r >= 3, and exhibits two explicit barriers showing why matching-tree decoders fail past support 2m^2 (c=1/18 > 1/36, constant Nash regret 1/12) and why chance-selected parallel matching branches stall at support m^2.
strengths: Clean and exact unscaled-simplex column-Hadamard argument in Theorem 1(b) that simultaneously eliminates tree-wide denominator multiplication (via path-LCM L) and halves the exponent of K relative to Cheval et al.

Polynomial-time effective payoff-deviation rank compression K_eff in Theorem 2(a) fits seamlessly into Algorithm 1's sequential prefix-expansion and Caratheodory BFS, collapsing quadratic support to linear whenever payoff rank r_i = O(1).

Complete characterization of b-ary matching trees in Theorem 3(b), discovering that ternary trees (b=3) match the optimal node slope 6 while halving the number of matching information sets, whereas binary trees (b=2) uniquely minimize leaf count and yield kappa_N totality for all r >= 3.

Insightful structural barriers in Theorem 3(d): the Battle of the Sexes correlated NFCE at support 2m^2 (c = 1/18) and the 2q-player synchronized matching NFCE at support m^2 sharply explain the limits of matching-tree hardness reductions.

Exceptional verification hygiene: 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems with zero sorry and zero Classical.choice, AST-audited zero-float verifier, 16 SHA-256 certificates, and 56 passing adversarial tests.
weaknesses: The Lean 4 formalization proves the algebraic, combinatorial, and inequality cores of the theorems rather than formalizing full extensive-form game trees, sequence-form Gaussian elimination, LP duality, or Pinsker's inequality inside Lean; those algorithmic and game-theoretic components rest on the prose proofs and zero-float concrete instances (cert03, cert04, cert16).

In Theorem 2(a), the polynomial-time extraction of a basis for V_i^{dir} delegates sequence-form details to Koller-Megiddo / Cheval et al. Section 3.2 rather than explicitly writing out the reachability pruning and leaf-incidence mapping M_i(ker E_i), and cert04 computes r_1, r_2 by enumerating pure plans on a small tree rather than exercising the polynomial-time.
Tightness of the general-r Hadamard bound in Theorem 1(b) remains open beyond r = 2 (where Theorem 1(c) gives exact 4L determinant tightness and 1/(2L) gap realization).
